fixed_choices.target: ideal J(X) = ||(X - T) W_hat^T||^2 with T = X_ref C G^{-1}; L - J is independent of X
fixed_choices.metric: G = h_inv^{-1} - c I rebuilt from the parent state
fixed_choices.ridge: c = mean(diag(inverse)) - mean(diag(W_hat^T W_hat)); the two means are taken in different hooks, never the fused matrix
fixed_choices.candidate_set: one element of one natural 4-element group, mantissa code +-1 at fixed scale_factor/lv2/lv3
fixed_choices.accept_rule: exact quadratic over the whole per-row move; a rejected row does not move in that step

passes_note: K=2 is the L-EM2 card's own pre-registered primary arm; L-EM2 shipped the K=1 fallback because the fallback rule fired under the card's naive additive convention, and L-EM3 submits the primary. K was not re-selected after the fact and K in {3,4,...} was not scanned. The mechanism is monotone by construction -- every step's whole per-row move is re-verified against the exact full-row quadratic and a rejected row does not move -- so raising K carries time risk only, never accuracy risk.
declared_deviation: the candidate differs from the L-EM2 bytes by the registered `_EM1_PASSES = 1 -> 2` plus a rewrite of the 5-line comment above that constant into 8 lines explaining why the K=2 arm is being submitted. Comments do not execute, so the mechanism claim in section 2 ('only _EM1_PASSES changes') holds literally, but the wording 'L-EM2 byte-for-byte unchanged' does not. Kept and disclosed rather than reverted because the measured source_sha256 IS ea79a1c1: reverting would make every result JSON in this archive describe bytes other than the shipped ones.

time_projection.convention_resolved_by_v230_official: mid-card the user reported v230 (K=1, the same mechanism) officially at 292s. Naive additive predicted 281 + 6.5 + 6.0 = 294s (2s error); the fitted decomposition predicted 286.5s (5.5s error). The naive additive convention is 2.8x more accurate on this reading, which makes it the working convention for this mechanism family. This is a single data point against a regression with MAE 10.1s and it is specific to this mechanism; it is not a claim that the naive convention is globally better.

The risk profile is nevertheless better than when the card was written: the root is now the 292s v230, so a timeout closes this candidate only and does not take the root with it, which is what happened at v229.

local_decision_note: the tool's local_trend_gate is `delta_mean > 0 and L1 < 0.02`, an eligibility screen for small local trends; the tool's own policy states 'local eligibility is not promotion'. A mechanism that deliberately makes a large change exceeds that L1 by design. The signal that matters here is 288 positive / 0 negative / 48 zero out of 336.
